newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Mahathir welcomes back splinter group.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Mahathir welcomes back splinter group.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Tuesday accepted back into his party 200,000 members of a defunct rival group ahead of crucial party polls this week.
Mahathir tore open one of the 26 large boxes wheeled into the Putra World Trade Centre building containing the 200,000 applications from members of the dissolved Spirit of '46 party.

He then shook hands warmly with Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah, the former head of Spirit and once his arch political rival, as Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and top officials of the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) looked on.
Razaleigh, a former finance minister, left UMNO to found the rival Malay party after narrowly losing a leadership battle to Mahathir at the party's election convention in 1987.

The return of his arch rival to the fold on the eve of Thursday's UMNO convention dramatically strengthen's Mahathir's hold on the party. Mahathir has been prime minister and head of UMNO for the past 15 years.
"Since he (Mahathir) is president of the party, this will help strengthen not just him but the party," Razaleigh told Reuters as he waited for Mahathir to arrive for the ceremony.
"Definitely Mahathir, being the leader, will get our support. All negotiations (regarding the rejoining of Spirit members) were with him," Razaleigh added.
Education Minister Najib Tun Razak, a UMNO vice president, told Reuters: "It's a very auspicious day."
Najib's father and Malaysia's second prime minister, Tun Abdul Razak Hussin, brought Razaleigh into the government and gave him his first big break in UMNO.
UMNO is the main party in the National Front coalition that has governed Malaysia since its independence from Britain in 1957.

Political analysts say the UMNO polls are arguably more significant than general elections, which the National Front has always won easily. By political convention, the president and deputy president of UMNO become prime minister and deputy prime minister.
Mahathir and Anwar are unchallenged for the top two jobs in UMNO under a pact made at last year's convention.
But 185 candidates are contesting other positions, including three vice presidencies, 30 seats on the policy-making Supreme Council, and heads of the youth and women's wings of the party.
Political analysts tend to view the contests as a kind of proxy battle between the 70-year-old Mahathir and his ambitious and charismatic deputy, 49-year-old Anwar Ibrahim.
The UMNO leadership has decreed a total ban on campaigning for the party posts, which in previous years has seen candidates wining and dining convention delegates.
On Monday, the party disqualified seven candidates from contesting the elections for trying to buy votes and violating UMNO's blanket ban on campaigning for the polls.
